#3234 · task-existence-gate: wire or delete?

Neither. The premise was dispatcher-blindness: grepping hooks.json + the entries map misses sub-hooks that live inside a registered dispatcher.

✅ VERDICT: the gate has been LIVE since its creation commit (b9db69576, 2026-03-12) as a sub-hook of sync-task-dispatcher, it fires in real sessions, and its blocking branch has tests. Only CLAUDE.md's "unregistered" claim was wrong.

What the gate actually does (unchanged, now documented truthfully)

Agent spawn (PreToolUse)
  │
  ├─ Explore / general-purpose / Plan / guide / statusline
  │  or run_in_background: true ──────────────▶ silent pass
  │
  ├─ task registered for agent ────────────────▶ silent pass
  │
  ├─ no task + NO active pipeline ─────────────▶ advisory nudge
  │                                              "[Task Tracking] ... Consider TaskCreate"
  └─ no task + ACTIVE ork pipeline ────────────▶ BLOCK
                                                 "Create a task with TaskCreate first"

The one real defect: CLAUDE.md

- No hook enforces this (task-existence-gate.ts is unregistered),
  so it is your judgement call.
+ Enforcement is layered, not absent: task-existence-gate runs live as a
+ sub-hook of sync-task-dispatcher (advisory on un-tasked foreground agent
+ spawns, hard block inside active ork pipelines), and multi-step-task-nudge
+ covers 3+ step prompts. Non-agent multi-step work remains judgement.

Lesson for the next archaeologist: a hook absent from hooks.json + entries is only dead if no registered dispatcher imports it. Check git log -S before declaring a corpse.
